raw_response:
# C24 — Catalogue baseline B

I found four useful candidates for reducing repetitive initialization while preserving author control. The proposed applications below are design-transfer inferences; none is claimed to implement Swift's rules or to have been proved useful for this case.

1. **Project Lombok constructor annotations and Builder** — [constructor documentation](https://projectlombok.org/features/constructor), [builder documentation](https://projectlombok.org/features/Builder). Required-field assignment generation can coexist with handwritten constructors; a builder can expose a selected constructor or factory to clients. This suggests sharing mechanical assignment while preserving author-controlled construction. Signature collisions remain errors. The [changelog](https://projectlombok.org/changelog) dates constructor annotations to 2010-07-25 and stable Builder support to 2015-01-26, both before the cutoff. Builder.Default arrived on 2017-03-23 and is excluded from the pre-cutoff claim. Discovery: [Awesome Java Annotation Processing](https://github.com/gunnarmorling/awesome-annotation-processing).

2. **Immutables** — [primary guide](https://immutables.github.io/immutable.html). Generated immutable implementations can accept client-supplied attributes while the author defines default, derived and lazy state. This is a useful model for separating input properties from implementation state without making the finished value mutable. A caveat is that non-public attributes can still appear as public builder inputs, so visibility alone does not establish the desired boundary. Historical availability of the selected features is **unknown**: the live guide was opened, but no dated pre-cutoff version was verified. Discovery: [Awesome Java Annotation Processing](https://github.com/gunnarmorling/awesome-annotation-processing).

3. **Sundrio builder generator** — [primary builder documentation](https://github.com/sundrio/sundrio/blob/main/annotations/builder/readme.md). Generating a builder for a selected constructor, excluding named properties and supporting inherited fields could centralize construction and reduce repeated caller setup for immutable objects and object graphs. The existing implementation requires getters plus setters or a matching constructor, with exact property/argument type matching. This leaves constructor-body invariants under author control but does not itself establish Swift definite-initialization semantics. Historical availability is **unknown** because only live documentation was verified. Discovery: [Awesome Java Annotation Processing](https://github.com/gunnarmorling/awesome-annotation-processing).

4. **attrs field declarations and initialization hooks** — [primary initialization guide](https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/init.html). Declarative fields, generated initialization and post-init hooks show how automatic assignments can compose with author-written derived state. Frozen instances offer runtime immutability, with a special assignment operation needed inside post-init. This is **later evidence**: the [changelog](https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/changelog.html) dates excluded-field default initialization to 2016-05-23, frozen support to 2016-08-30 and post-init hooks to 2016-11-24, all after 2016-01-13, although the package itself first released in 2015. Discovery: [Awesome Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vinta/awesome-python/master/README.md).

The evidence favors examining selective assignment generation, constructor delegation through generated builders, and separate declarations for supplied versus derived state. These are mechanisms to compare against the problem constraints, not a recommendation to port any library unchanged. Google Auto was discovered and its overview opened, but deeper AutoValue verification failed, so it is not included as a candidate.
